newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares end firm, seen tracking sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares end firm, seen tracking sideways.

text.p: Slovenia's SBI index rose 0.44 percent on subdued demand and traders forecast shares would drift sidewards until the end of August.
"We cannot expect foreign demand to stay as strong as in the past two days throughout August so I expect the index to remain around the same level to the end of the month," one trader said.
"This could be a good time to buy shares because analysts belive new foreign investors will come to Slovenia in the Autumn which will push prices up significantly," he added.
The SBI index rose 6.93 points to 1564.49.
Health resort operator Terme Catez was the most actively traded share, rising 3.19 percent to 12.930 tolars on volume of 4,764 shares.
Analysts said Terme was expected to deliver good business results this year but noted that its growth potential was limited due to a lack of interest by foreign investors in the stock.
Overall 11 shares rose, three were unchanged, five fall and nine were untraded. Turnover fall to 163.7 million tolars from 229.6 million.

Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, closing 10 percent higer at 10,890 tolars on volume of eight shares but traders said its gains could be short-lived because of poor liquidity of the stock.
Food company Droga led the decliners, dropping 2.12 percent to 32,300 on volume of 40 shares.
"Droga will probably rebaund as early as this week because this is a profitable company of interest to international and domestic investors," an analyst said.
